es.summary: Una cuenta distinta de la cuenta de servicio esperada usó SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege sobre la base de datos del Service Control Manager (ServicesActive). Suele indicar que alguien abrió un handle privilegiado al SCM, a menudo de forma remota, para manipular servicios.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos 4674 de Security con ObjectType 'SC_MANAGER OBJECT', ObjectName 'ServicesActive' y PrivilegeList 'SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege'. Excluye solo el caso en que SubjectLogonId es 0x3e4 (NETWORK SERVICE) y ProcessName termina en \Windows\System32\services.exe.
es.why_it_matters: Con un handle privilegiado al SCM se pueden crear, modificar o iniciar servicios que corren como SYSTEM. Esto corresponde a T1548 (abuso de mecanismos de control de elevación) y es habitual en ejecución remota tipo PsExec y en movimiento lateral.
triage_steps: Identifique SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName y SubjectLogonId. Confirme si la cuenta es administrativa y si se espera que gestione servicios en este host.
Busque el evento 4624 con el mismo TargetLogonId para obtener LogonType, IpAddress y WorkstationName. Un LogonType 3 apunta a acceso remoto al SCM.
Revise ProcessName y ProcessId. Que aparezca services.exe con un LogonId de usuario sugiere una conexión remota por RPC; otro binario implica uso local.
En el mismo host, dentro de +/- 15 minutos, busque eventos 7045, 4697 o 7040 (servicios creados o modificados) y 5145 con acceso al pipe svcctl en IPC$.
Revise eventos 4688 o la telemetría del EDR en busca de sc.exe, PsExec, binarios en ADMIN$ o servicios con rutas inusuales.
Desde la IP de origen, busque el mismo patrón contra otros hosts y revise si hay alertas previas para el usuario o el origen.
false_positives: Administradores que gestionan servicios de forma remota con services.msc, sc.exe o PowerShell desde estaciones de administración.
Herramientas de despliegue o gestión, como SCCM o agentes de inventario, que instalan o configuran servicios.
Escáneres de vulnerabilidades autenticados que consultan el SCM con credenciales privilegiadas.
response_steps: Confirme con el dueño de la cuenta o con el equipo de TI si la actividad estaba autorizada y coincide con un cambio registrado.
Si no estaba autorizada, aísle el host desde el EDR y deshabilite o restablezca la cuenta involucrada.
Identifique los servicios creados o modificados. Preserve sus binarios y su configuración como evidencia antes de deshabilitarlos o eliminarlos.
Revise el host de origen y los demás destinos en busca de movimiento lateral. Rote las credenciales expuestas y restaure los servicios legítimos.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel medio es adecuado: la operación da control a nivel SYSTEM y es común en movimiento lateral, aunque la administración legítima de servicios la produce con frecuencia.

en.summary: An account other than the expected service account used SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege on the Service Control Manager database (ServicesActive). This usually means someone opened a privileged SCM handle, often remotely, to manipulate services.
en.what_it_detects: Security event 4674 with ObjectType 'SC_MANAGER OBJECT', ObjectName 'ServicesActive' and PrivilegeList 'SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege'. It excludes only the case where SubjectLogonId is 0x3e4 (NETWORK SERVICE) and ProcessName ends with \Windows\System32\services.exe.
en.why_it_matters: A privileged SCM handle lets you create, change or start services that run as SYSTEM. This maps to T1548 (Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism) and is typical of PsExec-style remote execution and lateral movement.
triage_steps: Identify SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName and SubjectLogonId. Confirm whether the account is administrative and expected to manage services on this host.
Find the 4624 event whose TargetLogonId matches to get LogonType, IpAddress and WorkstationName. LogonType 3 points to remote SCM access.
Check ProcessName and ProcessId. services.exe with a user LogonId suggests a remote RPC connection; any other binary means local use.
On the same host within +/- 15 minutes, look for events 7045, 4697 or 7040 (services created or changed) and 5145 access to the svcctl pipe on IPC$.
Review 4688 events or EDR telemetry for sc.exe, PsExec, binaries dropped in ADMIN$ or services with unusual paths.
Search for the same pattern from the source IP against other hosts, and check for earlier alerts on the user or the source.
false_positives: Administrators managing services remotely with services.msc, sc.exe or PowerShell from admin workstations.
Deployment or management tools, such as SCCM or inventory agents, that install or configure services.
Authenticated vulnerability scanners that query the SCM with privileged credentials.
response_steps: Confirm with the account owner or IT that the activity was authorized and matches a recorded change.
If it was not authorized, isolate the host through the EDR and disable the account or reset its password.
Identify services that were created or changed. Preserve their binaries and configuration as evidence before you disable or remove them.
Check the source host and other targets for lateral movement. Rotate exposed credentials and restore legitimate services.
en.severity_rationale: Medium fits: the operation gives SYSTEM-level control and is common in lateral movement, but legitimate service administration triggers it often.

positive.description: Domain user's network logon opens a privileged SCM handle through services.exe (remote SCM access)
Local admin uses sc.exe, which triggers the privileged operation from a process other than services.exe

negative.description: NETWORK SERVICE (0x3e4) operation through services.exe, excluded by the filter
User operation on the SCM database with a different privilege (SeSecurityPrivilege), so the selection does not match
